competences: The learner identifies key facts about the government of uganda.
The learner explains information about Meaning of government and its organs using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes government, organs, arms of government.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the government of uganda.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Meaning of government and its organs.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the government of uganda.
materials: Chart showing the government of uganda
Primary Five SST reference on Meaning of government and its organs
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the government of uganda. They ask "Give one achievement made by the NRM government in Uganda." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the government of uganda
steps.content: Establishment of many government and private universities e.g. Mbarara university, Bugema university, Mbale university , KIU etc Corruption in some government departments. Inspector general of government (IGG) In which one way did Amin’s government violate human rights The National (central) government. Local council I Village Cell LC I They are all under the National government. This is the government that bears all the major responsibilities towards the people in a country. Differences between the central government and local government Central government Local government It is one government. There are many local governments.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the government of uganda on the chalkboard, including "Establishment of many government and private universities e.g. Mbarara university, Bugema university, Mbale university , KIU etc; Corruption in some government departments.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about the government of uganda
steps.content: This is the ruling organ of the government It is the organ of the government which is responsible for the day today running of the affairs of the country. It implements government policies. The executive , legislative and judiciary are the arms of the government, under what arm of the government do the following belongs: This is the money that the government collects from various sources. Income is the money earned by the government or someone (people) This is the money spend by the government through the provision of various social services required by the people. Loans Qn. Mention the major source of government revenue Tax is the money a person or company is asked by the government to pay OR
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the government of uganda on the chalkboard, including "This is the ruling organ of the government; It is the organ of the government which is responsible for the day today running of the affairs of the country.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about the government of uganda
steps.content: Tax is the money paid to the government by the citizens , organizations and businessmen It has government organs A government is a group of people given powers to rule a country Or Local government is under the ministry of local government The highest local government unit is LC5 Central government is one government while local government has many local government Central government runs major hospitals while local government controls dispensaries and health centres. Central government builds major roads while local government maintains feeder roads A civil servant is a person employed and paid by the government.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the government of uganda on the chalkboard, including "Tax is the money paid to the government by the citizens , organizations and businessmen; It has government organs". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Give one achievement made by the NRM government in Uganda. | Why did the government of president Museveni introduce UPE? | Name the laws that are used at local government. | Mention the types of government in Uganda. | Why is the government of Uganda dividing the country into many districts?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Give one achievement made by the NRM government in Uganda." and "Why did the government of president Museveni introduce UPE?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the government of uganda, asks "Give one achievement made by the NRM government in Uganda." and follows up with "Why did the government of president Museveni introduce UPE?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Give one achievement made by the NRM government in Uganda." and "Why did the government of president Museveni introduce UPE?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government."
